title: About
text: Hi! My name is Ella Cave, I am a junior student at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln studying Sports Media Communications and Broadcasting, minoring in Hospitality. I am interested in a career in sports media that includes either broadcasting or digital media. While being at UNL I have been able to write game stories, cover sporting events, and much more. I also have experience in social media through working with Hurrdat Sports as a Social Media Intern. I like to share stories about athletes, teams, and people behind just sports. Outside of school I enjoy hanging out with friends and family, being involved in Alpha Omicron Pi, and going to sports events.

title: What Makes a Successful College Basketball Team?
text:
This is a story about Women’s College Basketball and how the University of Nebraska-Omaha compares to other college basketball teams.
Scoring points is one of the biggest ways teams win games, but it isn’t the only thing that contributes to a win. A team’s defense and ability to handle the basketball can also create a huge difference in a game. Now, in women’s college basketball, some teams score a lot more points on average than other teams, but does that mean they are more successful than other lower-scoring teams?
For this project, I wanted to look at women’s college basketball team stats from the 2025-26 season because I wanted to see what stats might be related to the success of teams. I also want to look at the average points scored, the average points teams allow, and their turnover margin. Then connect that to how the University of Nebraska-Omaha women’s basketball team compares to others.
My first chart is a bar chart talking about the women’s college basketball teams with the highest average points and how UNO differs from them.

  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() + 
  labs(
    x="Teams", 
    y="Average Points Per Game", 
    title="How Does UNO's Average Points Per Game Compare to the Highest-Scoring Teams?", 
    subtitle="Average points per game for the top 15 scoring teams in Women's College Basketball, with Omaha highlighted in red.", 
    caption="Source: Sports-Reference | By Ella Cave"
    ) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size=8),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
  )









If you look at the chart above, you can see that there’s a big difference between the top 15 scoring teams and UNO. The top teams are averaging 75 + points per game, and UNO is averaging a little more than 50. This chart shows that UNO scores a lot less per game than the top 15 teams. As I said before scoring does help team win games, but doesn’t mean they are successful all together. Before we think of everything all together, let’s look at a scatterplot comparing UNO’s and the top 15 teams average points scored and average points allowed. This will show whether they have strong defenses and offenses.

The scatterplot shows how the top 15 scoring teams and UNO compare in offense and defense through the points they allowed and points they scored. The top 15 teams on the right side show that they are scoring more and are letting their opponents fewer points. This shows that having a strong offense doesn’t always mean a team has the strongest defense.
As you can see, there is a red dot; that is UNO. UNO has scored a lot fewer points than the top 15 teams, and they have allowed more points to opponents. UNO doesn’t have the same outcome as the top-scoring teams in women’s college basketball, as you can tell because they don’t have a very high scoring percentage. But I will say the points scored and points allowed are still not the only stats that can help a team be successful. One more stat I want to look at is the turnover margin for teams and how well a team can take care of the ball.

turnovers <- wbb_team_box_2026 |> 
  group_by(team_location) |> 
  summarise(
    avg_turnovers = mean(total_turnovers),
    avg_points_scored = mean(team_score),
    total_wins = sum(team_winner)
  )

    aes(x=avg_turnovers, y=avg_points_scored, size=total_wins),

The chart shows that teams with fewer turnovers and higher scoring averages have more wins. UNO is highlighted and looks to be a little below average compared to the rest of the teams. Although UNO isn’t turning the ball over that much, they still have a lower scoring average. This shows that taking care of the ball does help teams win.
After looking at the bar chart, scatterplot, and bubble chart, I think that there is more than one specific thing that makes a successful college basketball team. Now, scoring points, having a strong defense, and limiting turnovers can really make a difference in being a successful team. Overall, for teams that can succeed in all three things and turn those good stats into actual wins can have a better chance at being successful.
